newsitem.title: USA: Tandy CEO says business good, not robust.
newsitem.headline: Tandy CEO says business good, not robust.

text.p: Tandy Corp chief executive officer John Roach said the consumer electronics industry has improved in recent months and Tandy's business was showing steady, but not robust, growth.
"Business is good; I wouldn't describe it as robust," Roach told reporters after the company's annual meeting in Fort Worth.

"As a whole, we probably feel a lot better and a lot more confident about the consumer electronics industry now than we might have last year, when the industry was facing a lot of challenges," Roach said.

Tandy President Leonard Roberts said consumer electronics and audio/video products are still showing weakness but said Tandy's core products -- telecommunications and parts and accesories at its chain of RadioShack stores -- are "very healthy and growing very significantly".

He said those core products account for about 57 percent of Tandy's total business with audio/video products accounting for 19 percent. Computers and personal electronics each make make up 12 percent of revenues.

Roach has come under heavy pressure in recent months from dissident shareholders who blame him for the company's poor revenues and share price performance. The company decided last December to shut down all 19 of its Incredible Universe electronics superstores, all of its 53 McDuff home electronics stores and 21 of its 113 Computer City stores.
But there was no public dissent at the shareholders' meeting and all board members were re-elected with more than 85 percent support.
Roach said Tandy was focusing on its successful RadioShack chain and would open 100 company-owned RadioShacks this year as well as 200 dealer-owned stores in small towns.
A huge advertising campaign set to begin September 22 will draw attention to Tandy's alliance with Sprint Corp, under which Sprint is setting up stores inside all 6,800 RadioShacks.

Tandy also plans to open five or six Computer City stores this year and is considering opening up a small stand-alone chain of home electronics, parts and accesories stores aimed at engineers, technicians and serious electronics enthusiasts.
